source_evidence.observation: The remark says that the constant 2 occurring in some properties of Proposition 2.5.2 has no special meaning and may be replaced by any other absolute constant greater than 1.

For an arbitrary random variable X, the proposition declares properties (i)-(iv) equivalent, with positive parameters K_i comparable up to an absolute constant factor; the standalone bound constant 2 occurs in the tail bound in (i) and in the exponential-moment bound in (iv).
Parameter equivalence means that an absolute C exists such that property i with parameter K_i implies property j with K_j at most C K_i for any two listed properties.
When E X = 0, properties (i)-(iv) are also equivalent to the all-real-lambda MGF property (v).

source_evidence.anchor: Proof of Proposition 2.5.2, implications (iv) to (i), (iii) to (v), and (v) to (i)
source_evidence.observation: The proof exhibits the structural roles of the two bounds: an exponential-square moment bound produces a tail-prefactor bound via Markov's inequality, while the centered linear MGF property produces a two-sided tail bound.

binders: X is the arbitrary (real-valued) random variable inherited from Proposition 2.5.2 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening sentence; real-valued operations are displayed in items (i)-(v)).
A is any fixed absolute numerical constant satisfying A > 1 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3, phrase 'any other absolute constant that is larger than 1').
hypotheses: For the equivalence of properties (i)-(iv), no centering hypothesis is imposed on X (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening sentence and items (i)-(iv)).
The extension of the equivalence to property (v) has the additional hypothesis E X = 0 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2 moreover clause).
conclusions: Proposition 2.5.2 remains valid when the standalone numerical bound 2 in property (i), P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K_1^2), and the standalone numerical bound 2 in property (iv), E exp(X^2/K_4^2) <= 2, are replaced by A > 1 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3, read with PDF page 13; printed page 24, items (i) and (iv)).

Thus the A-modified tail, moment-growth, quadratic-MGF, and one-point exponential-square-moment properties are equivalent, with their positive scale parameters comparable up to absolute constant factors in the sense of Proposition 2.5.2 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3; PDF page 13; printed page 24, proposition opening paragraph and footnote 4).

If E X = 0, the same A-modified properties are also equivalent to property (v), namely existence of K_5 > 0 such that E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K_5^2 lambda^2) for every real lambda (PDF page 13; printed page 24, moreover clause and item (v), together with PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).
definitions_and_conventions: Modified property (i): there exists K_1 > 0 such that P{|X| >= t} <= A exp(-t^2/K_1^2) for every t >= 0 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (i), with the replacement authorized by Remark 2.5.3 on PDF page 15; printed page 26).
Property (ii): there exists K_2 > 0 such that ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 sqrt(p) for every p >= 1 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (ii)).
Property (iii): there exists K_3 > 0 such that E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K_3^2 lambda^2) whenever |lambda| <= 1/K_3 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (iii)).

Modified property (iv): there exists K_4 > 0 such that E exp(X^2/K_4^2) <= A (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (iv), with the replacement authorized by Remark 2.5.3 on PDF page 15; printed page 26).
Under E X = 0, property (v): there exists K_5 > 0 such that E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K_5^2 lambda^2) for every lambda in R (PDF page 13; printed page 24, moreover clause and item (v)).

The phrase 'parameters differ ... by at most an absolute constant factor' is defined by footnote 4 as pairwise implication with K_j <= C K_i for an absolute C (PDF page 13; printed page 24, footnote 4).
implicit_context: Remark 2.5.3 is not a standalone tail estimate; it modifies the equivalent-property characterization in Proposition 2.5.2 immediately preceding it (PDF page 15; printed page 26, placement directly after the proof of Proposition 2.5.2 and explicit reference to that proposition).

The relevant occurrences of 2 are the leading constant in property (i) and the right-hand threshold in property (iv), rather than exponents, subscripts, or proof-specific numerical inequalities (PDF page 13; printed page 24, structural comparison of items (i)-(iv), and PDF page 15; printed page 26, phrase 'appears in some properties').

'Absolute constant' means a fixed numerical constant independent of X and the variables t, p, and lambda; this is the chapter's convention as reflected by Proposition 2.5.2 and footnote 4 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, opening paragraph and footnote 4).

details: The replacement concerns the two standalone bound values 2 in properties (i) and (iv) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, items (i) and (iv); PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).
The permitted replacement is an arbitrary fixed absolute constant strictly greater than 1 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).
The modified tail estimate is two-sided through |X| and holds for every real threshold t >= 0 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (i), modified by Remark 2.5.3 on PDF page 15; printed page 26).

The L^p bound is uniform over p >= 1; the quadratic MGF bound is local in lambda with |lambda| <= 1/K_3; and the centered linear MGF bound is global over lambda in R (PDF page 13; printed page 24, items (ii), (iii), and (v)).
The modified property (iv) is a one-point exponential-square integrability bound at scale K_4 (PDF page 13; printed page 24, item (iv), modified by Remark 2.5.3 on PDF page 15; printed page 26).
Mean zero is required only for adjoining property (v) to the equivalence; it is not a hypothesis for equivalence of (i)-(iv) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, proposition opening and moreover clause).
The source's notion of equivalence includes comparability of the existential scale parameters up to an absolute multiplicative factor (PDF page 13; printed page 24, opening paragraph and footnote 4).
Remark 2.5.3 asserts invariance of this characterization under changing the fixed bound constant from 2 to another absolute value greater than 1 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).

undebatable_constraints: The replacement bound A must be an absolute numerical constant and must satisfy A > 1, not merely A >= 1 (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).

The changed occurrences are the leading tail prefactor in property (i) and the exponential-square expectation threshold in property (iv) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, items (i) and (iv), read with PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).

Property (i) remains quantified over all t >= 0, property (ii) over all p >= 1, property (iii) over |lambda| <= 1/K_3, and property (v) over all lambda in R (PDF page 13; printed page 24, items (i), (ii), (iii), and (v)).
Every K_i appearing in its corresponding property is existentially quantified and strictly positive (PDF page 13; printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and items (i)-(v)).
The mean-zero hypothesis is necessary to include property (v) in the equivalence but is absent from the equivalence of properties (i)-(iv) (PDF page 13; printed page 24, moreover clause).

The remark preserves an equivalence of sub-gaussian characterizations, not equality of the numerical parameters or an exact claim that one unchanged K_i works in every property (PDF page 13; printed page 24, opening paragraph and footnote 4; PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3).

ambiguities.issue: The remark does not say whether the comparison constant C for the K_i may depend on the newly chosen absolute bound A.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3 only says A may be any other absolute constant greater than 1, while PDF page 13; printed page 24, footnote 4 states parameter comparability for the original formulation.
ambiguities.impact: The qualitative equivalence for each fixed A > 1 is clear, but the source does not explicitly claim a comparison factor uniform as A varies arbitrarily close to 1 or becomes arbitrarily large.

ambiguities.issue: The terse wording does not explicitly distinguish simultaneous use of one replacement value A in both properties from choosing separate absolute constants greater than 1 for properties (i) and (iv).
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3 uses the singular phrase 'any other absolute constant' while referring collectively to the constant 2 in 'some properties'.
ambiguities.impact: The most literal contract uses one fixed A in both modified occurrences; allowing two independently fixed constants greater than 1 is a natural extension but is not stated verbatim.

contract_plain_english: For any random variable X and any fixed absolute numerical constant A > 1, the equivalent sub-gaussian characterizations in Proposition 2.5.2 are unchanged if the leading 2 in the tail condition and the bound 2 in the one-point exponential-square moment condition are both replaced by A. The four uncentered conditions remain equivalent with comparable positive scale parameters, and when E X = 0 they remain equivalent to the global linear-MGF condition as well (PDF page 15; printed page 26, Remark 2.5.3, interpreted in the explicit context of Proposition 2.5.2 and footnote 4 on PDF page 13; printed page 24).
